newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended well up on the day, rising as German bond prices also firmed.
Swiss shares also hit record highs, with the blue chip Swiss Market Index setting an all-time high of 3,841.9.
Swiss Confederate bond futures briefly hit 115.75, its highest level since the contract high of 115.80 on October 9.
"The Conf is still strong, partly in sympathy with Bunds. At the moment, clients are buying. There was a lot of short-covering," said one Swiss bond trader.
He said however that the day session high of 115.75 was hit "for only two seconds -- and it was due to illiquidity."
He added prices turned after hitting highs in midafternoon, "and at that point there were a lot of sellers."

But the trader also believed that there was a good chance that the 115.80 high on the December contract could be retested, given that the futures price appeared cheap compared with the cheapest-to-deliver bond in the cash market.

The short end of the market has also been encouraged by the Swiss National Bank's latest 10-day reserves figures for early November released on Monday. The data showed a rise in sight deposits. An SNB spokesman also said Monday the data show the SNB remained flexible with respect to banks' liquidity needs.

Among new issues, Grande Dixence a launched a 125 million Swiss franc bond with a 4-1/4 percent coupon priced at 101.35, via SBC Warburg. The 12-year bond was quoted in late trade at minus 0.75/0.55 to yield 4.16 percent SBHC.
Dec Conf futures up 25 points at 115.50.
Dec Comi bond up 18 points at 110.43.
Mar Euro Swiss francs up seven points at 97.90.
